items.title: HDB resale prices down 0.2% in Q3 flash estimate
items.excerpt: The flash estimate points to a 0.2% fall in HDB resale prices in Q3 2026, the third consecutive quarterly decline. This is an early estimate, not the final quarterly release. For your own purchase or sale, compare similar flats and their condition rather than applying the headline change directly.

items.title: More automation planned for BTO construction from 2027
items.excerpt: HDB plans to introduce smart passenger and material hoists at about half of BTO sites tendered from 2027, and expand trials of floor-screeding robots to at least four more projects. These are planned construction improvements, rather than a change to the completion date of every existing project.

items.title: Higher income ceilings for eligible HDB buyers
items.excerpt: For HFE applications from 24 August 2026, the monthly household income ceiling rises to S$16,000 for eligible families buying a new subsidised flat, buying resale with the CPF Housing Grant, or taking an HDB loan. The corresponding ceiling for eligible singles aged 35 and above buying a subsidised flat or taking an HDB loan rises to S$8,000.

items.title: Next BTO launch moves to November 2026
items.excerpt: The next sales exercise has moved from October to November. HDB plans to offer about 7,960 flats across Bedok, Geylang, Sembawang, Tengah, Toa Payoh and Yishun, including Community Care Apartments in Toa Payoh. Buyers need a valid HFE letter when applying.

items.imageCaption: Housing display · Not a November project rendering

items.title: 15-month wait removed for certain private-property owners
items.excerpt: Private-property owners and former owners no longer face the 15-month wait when buying a non-subsidised HDB resale flat without an HDB loan. An HFE letter is still required. The separate 30-month wait for subsidised purchases or an HDB loan remains, so the financing route matters.

items.title: HDB resale prices fell 0.3% in Q2 2026
items.excerpt: HDB’s resale price index declined 0.3% in the second quarter, following a 0.1% fall in the first quarter. This is a market-wide measure: the price of an individual flat still depends on its location, remaining lease, condition and comparable transactions.
